I don't have any notes for you yet. My searches failed, and the research tool then stopped letting me run anything more in this session, so I never got to read a single page.

**What happened:**
- The first search for "Enduring Word Numbers 32 commentary" came back in a format my script didn't expect, and it crashed before showing any results.
- When I tried again to look at the raw results, the tool said I had used up my calls for this turn. The other tool I have can't reach the internet, so I couldn't work around it.

You asked me to report only what the pages actually say, with a URL for each point. Since I read nothing, writing notes from my own memory and attaching links I never opened would break that rule. So I've left the notes out entirely.

**What I'll do when you ask again (for example, "continue"):**
1. **Traditional reading, verse by verse:** the Enduring Word page on Numbers 32, and the Bible Hub and StudyLight pages for verses 22–42 (Gill, Ellicott, Pulpit Commentary, Matthew Henry), plus Precept Austin.
2. **Verse 23, "your sin will find you out":** this is the verse most likely to show differences between traditions. I'll look for sermons on it from spurgeon.org, desiringgod.org, gty.org, ligonier.org, wesley.nnu.edu and the Lutheran sites (lcms.org, 1517.org).
3. **Other views:** NET Bible notes on the place names and their renaming in verse 38, Havvoth-jair and Nobah (verses 41–42), and the half-tribe of Manasseh (verses 33 and 39–40). Also Bible Odyssey on the tribes east of the Jordan, and any Catholic or Orthodox comment on newadvent.org, catholic.com or oca.org.

I'll write up only what I can find and confirm, verse by verse with the URL for each point, and leave out anything I can't find.
